tears-of-joy.context: A laughing face with squeezed shut eyes, a wide open grin and a tear springing from each eye. Used in chats, reactions and comments to show that something is extremely funny.

melting-face.context: A smiling face that slumps down into a puddle, with a drip running down one cheek. Used for heat, embarrassment, dread or feeling overwhelmed in messages and reactions.

innocent-face.context: A smiling face with closed happy eyes and a halo floating over the head. Used to act innocent, show good behaviour or play angelic in chats and reactions.

adoring-face.context: A smiling face with closed eyes and three small hearts floating around the head. Used to express love, adoration, affection and gratitude in messages, cards and reactions.

zany-face.context: A goofy face with one big round eye, one small eye and the tongue hanging out of a crooked mouth. Used for silliness, wild fun and joking around in chats and reactions.

hugging-face.context: A smiling face with closed eyes and two open hands raised in front of the cheeks as if offering a hug. Used to send hugs, comfort, thanks and warm welcomes.

smirking-face.context: A face with half closed eyes glancing to the side and a lopsided smile raised at one corner. Used for smug, sly, flirty or suggestive remarks in chats.

unamused-face.context: A face with flat half lidded eyes looking sideways and a short mouth turned down at the ends. Used to show boredom, disapproval or being unimpressed by a joke or message.

eye-roll-face.context: A face with both pupils rolled up to the top of the eyes and a flat straight mouth. Used for exasperation, sarcasm and disbelief in replies and reactions.

lying-face.context: A face with a very long pointed nose sticking out to one side and a nervous wavy smile. Used for lies, fibs, fake news and dishonesty in chats, games and quizzes.

drooling-face.context: A dreamy face with closed eyes, a slack open mouth and a drop of drool running from one corner. Used for craving food or anything very desirable.

woozy-face.context: A tipsy face with one wide eye, one half closed eye, a wavy mouth and blushing cheeks. Used for feeling drunk, dizzy, giddy or out of it.

monocle-face.context: A face wearing a round monocle over one eye with the other brow raised and a thin chain hanging down. Used for scrutiny, curiosity and posh or fancy tones.

pleading-face.context: A face with huge round eyes holding big shine highlights, brows tilted up and a small frown. Used for begging, asking nicely or showing that something is touching or cute.

dotted-line-face.context: A face drawn only in a dashed outline with dotted eyes and mouth, as if fading from view. Used for feeling invisible, ignored, shy or wanting to disappear.

exhaling-face.context: A face with closed eyes blowing a small puff of air out from the mouth in a long sigh. Used for relief, tiredness, calming breaths and letting go of stress.

saluting-face.context: A face with a flat hand raised to the brow in a salute and a straight mouth. Used to show respect, acknowledge an order or say yes sir in a playful way.

flushed-face.context: A face with wide round eyes, a tiny round mouth and solid blush circles on both cheeks. Used for embarrassment, surprise and feeling flustered.

blushing-face.context: A smiling face with closed happy eyes, a soft smile and short diagonal blush lines on both cheeks. Used for flattered, shy and sweet happy feelings.

determined-face.context: A face with a headband tied around the forehead, sharp lowered eyes and a tight straight mouth, the knot ends flying to one side. Used for motivation, focus and fighting spirit.

pouting-face.context: A sulking face with lips pushed out into a pout, one puffed cheek and lowered brows. Used for sulking, mild annoyance and playful grumpiness.

fuming-face.context: An angry face with lowered brows and gritted teeth, with puffs of steam coming out of both sides of the head. Used for fury, frustration and being really mad.

cursing-face.context: An angry face with frowning brows and a bar of symbols covering the mouth. Used for swearing, censored words, profanity and outbursts of rage.

cross-eyed-face.context: A goofy face with both pupils turned inward toward the nose and an open grin. Used for silliness, confusion, dizziness and derpy humor.

gap-toothed-grin.context: A wide grinning face showing a row of upper teeth with a gap where one front tooth is missing. Used for kids, losing baby teeth, the tooth fairy and goofy smiles.

smiling-tear-face.context: A smiling face with happy upturned eyes and a single tear sliding down one cheek. Used for bittersweet moments, being touched, pride and smiling through pain.

holding-back-tears.context: A face with big glossy eyes brimming with tears, worried brows and a pressed, wobbly mouth. Used when trying not to cry, feeling moved, sad or overwhelmed.

face-in-clouds.context: A face half hidden behind a puffy cloud with only the eyes peeking over the top. Used for daydreaming, confusion, brain fog and having your head in the clouds.

knocked-out-face.context: A dazed face with crossed out eyes, a small open mouth and a round bump rising from the top of the head. Used for being knocked out, exhausted or beaten in games and chats.

injured-face.context: A face with a bandage wrapped around the top of the head, a plaster on one cheek and a small frown. Used for injuries, accidents, getting hurt and feeling beaten up.

cold-face.context: A freezing face with chattering zigzag teeth and a snowflake beside the head. Used for cold weather, winter, air conditioning and feeling chilly.

overheated-face.context: A hot face with droopy eyes, the tongue hanging out of the mouth and sweat drops on both cheeks. Used for hot weather, heatwaves, exhaustion and feeling overheated.

screaming-face.context: A long face with both hands pressed on the cheeks, wide eyes and a tall oval open mouth. Used for horror, fear, shock and dramatic panic.

confounded-face.context: A frustrated face with tightly squeezed eyes drawn as angle marks and a zigzag mouth. Used for frustration, stress, confusion and feeling overwhelmed.

nervous-laugh-face.context: A grinning face with closed curved eyes, a row of teeth and a single sweat drop on the forehead. Used for nervous laughter, awkward moments and relief after a close call.

jaw-drop-face.context: An astonished face with wide eyes and the jaw hanging far down, making a very long open mouth. Used for disbelief, amazement and being lost for words.

mind-blown-face.context: A face whose head bursts open at the top with a cloud blast rising above, and wide eyes below. Used for mind blown moments, amazement and shocking news.

puffed-cheeks-face.context: A face with round inflated cheeks, closed eyes and small pressed lips holding in a breath. Used for holding your breath, bloating, fullness and suppressed laughter.

duck-face.context: A selfie face with lips pushed forward into a pout and one eyebrow raised. Used for selfies, posing, sass and social media photos.

biting-lip-face.context: A face with raised worried brows and the upper teeth biting down on the lower lip. Used for nervousness, anticipation, temptation and flirting.

evil-grin-face.context: A scheming face with sharply slanted brows, narrow eyes and a wide toothy grin curling up at the corners. Used for mischief, evil plans, villains and pranks.

devil-face.context: A grinning round face with two small curved horns on top of the head and slanted eyes. Used for naughty behavior, mischief, temptation and Halloween.

cyborg-face.context: A face split down the middle, one half human with an eye and a smile, the other half metal plates with a round lens eye. Used for cyborgs, androids, AI and sci fi themes.

cute-monster-face.context: A round fuzzy edged monster with one big central eye, a small horn and two little fangs in a smile. Used for kids apps, games, Halloween and playful monster characters.

sun-with-face.context: A round sun disc with a calm smiling face in the middle and short rays all around. Used for sunny weather, good mornings, summer and cheerful moods.

sour-face.context: A puckered face with tightly squeezed eyes and small pursed lips beside a lemon wedge. Used for sour tastes, bitterness and the reaction to something tart or unpleasant.

see-no-evil-monkey.context: A monkey face with round ears and a muzzle, covering its eyes with both hands. Used for embarrassment, not wanting to look and playful oops moments.

hear-no-evil-monkey.context: A monkey face with wide eyes and a muzzle, pressing both hands over its ears. Used for not listening, ignoring gossip and blocking out noise.

speak-no-evil-monkey.context: A monkey face with round ears and wide eyes, covering its mouth with both hands. Used for secrets, saying too much, oops moments and keeping quiet.

grinning-cat-face.context: A cat face with pointed ears, whiskers and a wide open grin. Used for happy pets, cat lovers, playful joy and cheerful reactions.

crying-cat-face.context: A sad cat face with pointed ears, whiskers, an unhappy mouth and a tear running down one cheek. Used for sadness, disappointment and upset pets.

heart-eyes-cat-face.context: A cat face with pointed ears, whiskers, heart shaped eyes and a smile. Used for love, adoration, crushes and cat lovers.

weary-cat-face.context: A shocked cat face with pointed ears, round eyes, an open mouth and both paws raised to the cheeks. Used for shock, fear and horror in a playful way.

concentrating-face.context: A focused face with squinting eyes, lowered brows and the tip of the tongue poking out of one corner of the mouth. Used for concentration, hard work and careful effort.

yelling-face.context: A face with a huge open mouth and short shout lines bursting out in front of it. Used for shouting, yelling, loud announcements and angry rants.

wincing-face.context: A face with one eye squeezed shut, the other half open and clenched teeth pulled to one side. Used for pain, cringing, awkward moments and bracing for bad news.

hair-raising-face.context: A frightened face with wide eyes, a small open mouth and spiky hair standing straight up on end. Used for fright, horror stories, shocks and scary moments.

bubble-gum-face.context: A face with half closed eyes blowing a big round bubble of chewing gum. Used for boredom, casual attitude, sweets and playful cool vibes.

paper-bag-head.context: A paper bag pulled down over a head with a crinkled folded top, two cut out eye holes and a small mouth slit. Used for embarrassment, hiding, shame and anonymity.

fake-smile-mask.context: A sad face partly hidden behind a smiling mask held up in front of it on a stick. Used for hiding real feelings, masking, pretending to be fine and mental health topics.

mixed-feelings-face.context: A face split down the middle, one half smiling with a raised brow and the other half frowning. Used for mixed emotions, ambivalence, mood swings and bittersweet news.

emotion-wheel.context: A circle divided into wedge segments like a pie chart with a small smiling face in the centre. Used for feelings wheels, mood tracking, therapy and emotional check ins.

mood-ring.context: A finger ring with a large stone on top showing a small smiling face. Used for mood tracking, feelings, retro fashion and jewelry that changes colour with mood.

anger-symbol.context: Four curved bulging vein marks arranged in a cross, the cartoon sign for anger. Used in comics, manga, chats and reactions to show irritation or rage.

dizzy-symbol.context: A small star with a curling spiral trail swooping behind it. Used for dizziness, seeing stars, magic sparkle effects and things that spin.

looking-eyes.context: A pair of large eyes side by side with the pupils glancing to one side. Used for looking, watching, side eye, curiosity and drawing attention to something.

angry-speech-bubble.context: A jagged spiky speech bubble with an exclamation mark inside. Used for shouting, angry comments, outbursts and loud comic speech.

pixel-smiley.context: A smiley face built from square pixels, with a blocky circle outline, two square eyes and a stepped smile. Used for retro games, 8 bit art and nostalgic interfaces.

emotional-intelligence.context: A head in profile with a heart inside and small rays around the heart. Used for emotional intelligence, empathy, self awareness and mental health topics.

hannya-mask.context: A horned demon mask with two sharp horns, staring eyes and a wide mouth full of teeth and fangs, as used in Japanese Noh theatre. Used for Japanese culture, theatre, tattoos and demon themes.

okame-mask.context: A round smiling mask with full cheeks, crescent eyes, high dot brows and hair parted at the forehead. Used for Japanese festivals, good fortune, folk theatre and cultural topics.

hyottoko-mask.context: A comic mask with lips pursed to one side as if blowing, one eye larger than the other and a scarf knotted on top. Used for Japanese festivals, folk dance and comic theatre.

kabuki-face.context: A stage face with bold makeup stripes sweeping up from the eyes and brows to the temples and a downturned mouth. Used for Japanese kabuki theatre, stage makeup and drama.

peking-opera-mask.context: A painted opera face with a symmetric pattern, upswept wing brows, bold eye patches and an emblem on the forehead. Used for Chinese opera, stage makeup and cultural events.

kathakali-face.context: A painted dance face with a tall round crown behind the head, long painted eyes and a stiff ridged frame along the jaw. Used for Kathakali dance drama, Kerala and Indian classical arts.
